A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoStep by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison despite substantial methodological and experimental revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original sampling experiments on synthetic distributions and Bayesian posteriors, including sampler comparisons, jitter ablations and sampling diagnostics in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 reports original acceptance-probability, tuning, robustness and benchmark experiments in Section 5 and Appendix B, together with reference-sample analyses.

M1.justification: V2 removes Gaussian step-size jitter and its adaptation, prescribing the zero-jitter case already permitted in v1. Section 3.2 and Algorithm 3 replace averaging selected step sizes with median log-step-size tuning. The reported RWMH proposal also changes from x + theta*z to x + theta*M^{-1}*z. These revise the sampling procedure, beyond clarification or renaming.

E1.justification: V2 adds Laplace and Cauchy targets and the Gliese 229 orbital posterior, while removing banana and sonar/horseshoe experiments. Gaussian testing shifts from multivariate ablations to one-dimensional tests. Funnel, mRNA and Kilpisjarvi coverage is retained; Kilpisjarvi already appeared in v1's appendix and jitter experiments.

E2.justification: The adaptive comparison expands from NUTS and hit-and-run slice sampling in v1 Appendix B.8/Figure 13 to those methods plus adaptive RWMH, adaptive MALA and delayed-rejection HMC in v2 Section 5.4/Figure 5. Fixed-step RWMH/MALA comparisons remain, while the corresponding HMC comparison disappears.

E3.justification: V2 replaces the principal autocorrelation/known-moment minESS metric with KSESS using reference CDFs and 40 batches; supplementary ESS uses Geyer's estimator. New protocols include 20-round tuning and million-step robustness runs across initial step sizes from 10^-7 to 10^7, unlike v1's tuned-step multipliers and default minESS > 100 stopping criterion. Appendix B.1 also changes funnel variance, scale and dimensional settings.

E4.justification: V1's jitter ablations, jitter-convergence analysis and fixed-versus-tuned jitter tests are removed. V2 substantially revises the symmetry analysis into acceptance-versus-state-norm tests across three tail behaviors, and adds initial-step-size tuning and robustness analyses with cost, acceptance and jump-distance diagnostics. The comparative mRNA pair-plot case study and Gaussian-hole scatter plots are also removed.

E5.justification: V1 Section 5 specifies 30 independent trials by default; v2 omits this statement without supplying an equivalent trial count for its benchmark summaries. This reduces statistical reporting detail without establishing that fewer runs were performed. Both versions retain the three-chain calibration and 2% error-tolerance description for cost-scaling estimates.

E6.justification: Substantial jitter and AutoStep-HMC results disappear. V2 Figures 1–4 report RWMH acceptance above 10% across the tested state norms, tuned initial step sizes stabilizing around 1 despite widely varying initialization, and robustness/cost trends. Figures 5 and 9 provide revised adaptive-comparison results. Changed methods, metrics and target settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds Proposition 4.9's expected selector-cost bound and Corollary 4.10's logarithmic dependence on initial step size, with proofs in Appendix A. It revises termination assumptions and removes the positive-jitter alternative from Corollary 4.6. Appendix D introduces mathematical definitions and a heuristic derivation of KSESS. The earlier energy-jump bound is retained as Proposition 4.11.

C1.justification: V2 promotes expected computational cost and quantitative robustness to initial step size into central contributions in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. V1 established finite termination and energy-jump bounds without this cost claim. The empirical pitch shifts toward robustness of the simplified selector, while the main invariance, irreducibility, aperiodicity and competitiveness claims remain.

C2.justification: V1's recommendations that tuned jitter prevents catastrophic failures and its interpretation of erratic NUTS behavior on mRNA disappear. V2 explains robustness through logarithmic adaptation cost and discusses its efficiency penalty. Appendix B.4 adds qualifications that MALA acceptance still declines in the tails and that large Cauchy jumps can reflect rare extremes rather than good mixing.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents several comparator settings, explicit Kilpisjarvi prior parameters, orbital-model access information and reference-sample counts in Appendices B–C. V1's detailed hit-and-run configuration and AutoStep-HMC leapfrog tuning instructions disappear. The main code/data access link remains unchanged. Newly disclosed settings alone do not establish changes to previously used implementations.

R1.justification: V2 expands the existing discussion of concurrent Gibbs self-tuning work, explicitly acknowledging the same general augmentation technique while distinguishing its selector and theoretical analysis. It adds focused references for adaptive comparators, orbital modeling and the Kolmogorov diagnostic, and removes references associated with discarded experiments. The Modi citation's year update concerns the same work.

P1.justification: Section 5 is substantially rewritten and reorganized around symmetry, initial-step-size tuning, robustness and adaptive comparisons. The adaptive comparison moves from the appendix into the main narrative. Method explanations and introduction paragraphs are revised, and the experimental appendix is reorganized with new reference-plot and diagnostic appendices. Much of the background and augmented-space exposition remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are extensively replaced: v1's explanatory schematic, jitter plots and comparative sampler pair plots give way to robustness curves, revised benchmark summaries and five reference-sample pair plots. Table 1 changes from two blocks of model configurations to one compact table. Figure placement, legends, plotting styles and document layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for automatic adaptation: v1 established finite termination, whereas v2 quantifies expected computational overhead and connects its logarithmic bound to systematic initialization tests. Expanded comparator coverage and a documented CDF-based diagnostic also improve evaluation of the central claims. KSESS remains heuristic, and removing HMC/other benchmarks and the independent-trial count creates tradeoffs, but the stronger theoretical support and targeted validation provide a substantial overall gain.
